venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU — Faulkner’s 11, White’s nickel
dek: What the box will not tell you. Personnel Faulkner actually played. The three answers he kept calling. The front White lined up, and why FAU still moved it. Broadcast condensed — not All-22.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — 20:11 SEC condensed game sat (Charles Drive upload). Broadcast condensed, not All-22, not a 67-snap chart. Charles has not approved publish. Fan rail stays empty.

sources.label: Official box / starters (personnel card + stats support)

headline: Faulkner’s card says 12. Saturday he lived in 11 — shotgun, three wide, Baugh, one tight end. White’s card is a 4-2-5 nickel with stand-up edges. That is the front we kept seeing. FAU beat the cushion, not the scheme name.

offense.kicker: Buster Faulkner — personnel and the three answers
offense.body:
Personnel first, because the box does not speak it.

11 personnel means one running back, one tight end, three receivers. 12 means one back, two tight ends, two receivers. Empty means nobody in the backfield — five out.

Florida’s official starters are 12: Baugh in the backfield, Amir Jackson and Lacota Dippre at tight end, Eric Singleton Jr. and Dallas Wilson outside. That is the heavier card. On this cut, that is not what they lived in. The snap we kept seeing is 11: shotgun, 2x2 (two receivers to each side), Baugh next to Aaron Philo (No. 12), one tight end on the line, and Vernell Brown III (No. 1) or Bailey Stockton (No. 3) or TJ Abrams (No. 4) as the third wide. Singleton starts. Brown does the damage. That is the tell. Faulkner wants width vs a spread defense, not two tight ends in a phone booth.

They huddle. On a 1st-and-10 early, they are set with the play clock in single digits. The condensed cut skips that. The official chart stamps “No Huddle-Shotgun.” Ignore both. Opening drive is 7 plays in 3:20. The Clark score is 8 plays in 4:47. That is a coach getting the call in, then playing.

The scheme on this tape is three answers, over and over.

First answer: give it to Jadan Baugh (No. 13). Inside zone — the line zone-blocks one way, Baugh reads the first hole, or he plants and bounces when it clogs. That is the 12-yard cut and the 7-yard bounce. When they want to finish, it is gap / power — a puller, pads down, through the pile. That is the 6-yard score. The 61 is the same family with a crease. Fourteen carries, 160 yards. The box says workhorse. The film says Faulkner’s early-down diet is Baugh, not a deep ball on first down.

Second answer: the quick game. Ball out now. Brown’s 49 is a short catch at midfield. First man misses. He runs. Wilson’s 19 and 15 are the same family — get it out, move the chains. Stockton’s 12 is a placed fade at the pylon, not a jump-ball prayer. Philo is 16-of-21 because the design is rhythm. He is not hunting heroes. That is why 9.3 yards per play is not “they just have athletes.” It is YAC after a simple throw, then one real shot.

Third answer: the shot. After FAU punches in, Faulkner max-protects and Philo throws the deep ball to Abrams down the right sideline — the 63. Brown later takes a 33 down the same sideline. When they want a vertical, they take it. They do not live there.

The changeups, so you can see them next week: empty at the 3, edges climb, Philo keeps (nobody in the backfield — that is the keep). Brown as a ball carrier, 14 yards left — they will manufacture a touch for the receiver. Luke Harpring (No. 15) in the middle for 19 — the tight end is in the pass game, not just a blocker. Duke Clark (No. 20) is the second-back closer, not a gadget. The one sneak we can call under center is 4th-and-1 at midfield.

What condensed still hides: every RPO read, 10 vs 11 vs 12 on every snap, the protection slide. We are not inventing those. We are telling you what kept showing up.
bullets: Card: 12 (Baugh, two TEs, Singleton, Wilson). Saturday: 11 — shotgun, 2x2, three wide.
Huddle pace. Play clock in single digits when they are set. Not a hurry-up identity.
Answer 1: Baugh zone and bounce, then power to finish. That is the early-down diet.
Answer 2: Quick game. Brown 49 is YAC after a short catch. Wilson moves the chains.
Answer 3: The shot. Max protect, Abrams 63. They take it. They do not live there.
Changeups: empty keep; Brown as a runner; Harpring in the middle; Clark as the closer.

defense.kicker: Brad White — the nickel, the edges, why they still moved it
defense.body:
Personnel first again.

White’s official starters vs FAU are a 4-2-5 nickel: four down (Jayden Woods and LJ McCray at end, Brendan Bett and DK Kalu inside), two linebackers (Myles Graham and Aaron Chiles), five DBs (Ben Hanks III and Cormani McClain at corner, Kanye Clark as the extra DB, Bryce Thornton and DJ Coleman at safety). 4-2-5 means two linebackers and an extra defensive back in the slot. It is built for spread. FAU is spread. That is the card, and that is the look we kept seeing.

The Saturday tell is the stand-up edge. Two hands in the dirt inside. Two ends who can rush or drop. That is Woods and McCray. When the quarterback bounces, that edge failed. Veltkamp’s 7-yard pylon score is that failure — Kamran James (No. 24) is in the picture, contain is gone.

He is not stuck in 4-down. On the opening 3rd-and-10 empty he shows 3-down, linebackers walking, then a four-man rush into a zone drop. Default rush on this tape is four. We did not see a blitz-happy night. We saw a front that waits for the quarterback to hold it.

The shell mixes one-high and two-high. Do not name Cover 3 from this camera. What you can see: corners play off. FAU lives on hitch, flat, and out. Thirty-four completions, 5.2 yards a throw. That is not explosives. That is the dink game vs a cushion. Kanye Clark is the STAR — the extra DB who has to take the slot and fit the alley. When that spot is late, Veltkamp gets the free access throw. That is how you give up 25 first downs and still get two interceptions.

What worked, and why: Coleman jumps the throwing lane on 3rd-and-10 when the ball comes out late — drive dies at the Florida 6. Dijon Johnson (No. 27) high-points a back-foot duck after A-gap heat. Graham leads the team with 10 tackles. That is the scrape — the linebacker filling the hole the lineman left. Jeramiah McCloud (8 tackles, 2 hurries) is the interior presence the box actually matches to the film.

What lost: Ethan Ervin in the phone booth on the goal line (the fit is packed and they still lose the plane). Veltkamp around the edge. Kelby Valsin (No. 2) stacks J’Vari Flowers (No. 6) on the fade. Same family as Stockton the other way. Bett’s strip is the fourth-quarter chart (Myles Johnson recovers). We are not inventing the stunt from this camera.

Sumrall said atrocious at times. The film version: the front is right for spread. The cushion and the edge are how 75-yard drives start. Campbell is also no-huddle shotgun. The STAR and the JACK have to be cleaner.
bullets: Card and Saturday: 4-2-5 nickel. Two LBs, extra DB in the slot (Kanye Clark).
Tell: 4-down, stand-up edges (Woods, McCray). Mixes 3-down on obvious pass.
Default rush is four. They wait for the hold. Coleman and Johnson are the reward.
Corners play off. FAU’s 34 completions at 5.2 YPA are hitch / flat / out, not bombs.
Graham (10) is the scrape. McCloud is the interior. Bett’s strip is the fourth.
Leaks: phone-booth dive, Veltkamp contain, Valsin fade vs Flowers.

specials.kicker: Specials — the one kick that was a call
specials.body: Patrick Durkin from 53, 4th-and-4, 2:06 of the first. That is a coach leaving the offense on the field and still taking the points from the opponent 35. Clean operation, 17–0. Kickoffs are touchbacks. Florida never punts. Unused punter is a box fact, not a film take.
bullets: Durkin 53 on 4th-and-4: they kept the offense out there, then took the points.
No Florida punt. Eleven kickoffs, ten touchbacks.

keys: Faulkner’s card is 12. Saturday he played 11: shotgun, 2x2, Baugh, one TE, three wide.
Three answers: Baugh zone/power, the quick game, one deep shot. They huddle.
White’s card is 4-2-5 nickel. Stand-up edges. Rush four. Mix the shell.
FAU moved it with hitch / flat / out vs off coverage — 34 catches, 5.2 a throw.
Who the film keeps: Baugh, Philo, Brown III, Wilson, Abrams, Clark, Coleman, Graham, Durkin.
Campbell is no-huddle shotgun. The STAR (slot) and the JACK (edge) are the jobs.

nextWeek.look: Campbell is the no-huddle shotgun team. Florida’s tape is 11-personnel huddle vs a 4-2-5. White has to win the slot and the edge. Faulkner will still be shotgun 11 — width, Baugh, then the quick game.
